findings.title: `sshQueueTransport` ignores the caller lifetime that `request` passes to it.

findings.body:
**Align the registry with the `makeQueueOps()` surface.**

`src/ops/review/registry.ts:601-608` registers `review.retry` and `review.drain`, but `makeQueueOps()` declares neither member. This can fail type-checking. The registry test also compares the sorted names and omits both entries, so the assertion fails. The order difference is not relevant because both arrays are sorted.
findings.title: Align the registry with the `makeQueueOps()` surface.

findings.body:
**Apply the round-1 gate to `lease.expectedHead`.**

The unconditional `lease.expectedHead` spread overrides the `round === 1` limit on `input.expectedHead`. From round 2 on, the loop can receive the original selection head. Once a round-1 commit moves the local HEAD, the head check before dispatch can refuse the run.

The child lease sets `expectedHead` to `child.selection.head` (`addressOwnership.ts:1185`). The loop checks the fetched worktree HEAD against `opts.expectedHead` before dispatch (`review-loop.ts:1004-1006`). On a mismatch it returns `needs-human` with `headRefused: true` and the reason `PR head changed before dispatch` (`review-loop.ts:1007-1010`).

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-                  ...(round === 1 && input.expectedHead
-                    ? { expectedHead: input.expectedHead }
+                  ...(round === 1 && (lease.expectedHead ?? input.expectedHead)
+                    ? { expectedHead: (lease.expectedHead ?? input.expectedHead)! }
                     : {}),
                   gh,
                   git,
                   registry:
                     deps.worktreeRegistry ??
                     lease.registry ??
                     fileWorktreeRegistry(resolve(journalDir, 'worktrees.json')),
-                  ...(lease.expectedHead ? { expectedHead: lease.expectedHead } : {}),
```

</details>
findings.title: Apply the round-1 gate to `lease.expectedHead`.
